title: Psychopathology: Phobias & Depression
welcome_lead: Mowrer says you learn fears two ways; Beck says depression sits in a triad.
meta_desc: A-Level Psychology phobias Mowrer two-process, depression Beck negative triad and Ellis ABC.
final_note: Behavioural for phobias, cognitive for depression — match the explanation to the disorder.

concepts.def: Mowrer 1947 — phobias acquired by classical, maintained by operant conditioning.
Wolpe gradual exposure paired with relaxation.
Immediate, prolonged exposure to feared stimulus until anxiety subsides.
Beck — negative views of self, world and future.
Faulty thinking like overgeneralisation or catastrophising.

walkthroughs.body_html: Mowrer (1947): phobias begin with classical conditioning (Little Albert paired a rat with a loud noise) and are maintained by operant conditioning — avoidance is negatively reinforced because anxiety reduces. Treatments break the cycle through exposure.

Systematic desensitisation (Wolpe 1958) climbs a hierarchy of feared situations paired with relaxation — reciprocal inhibition. Flooding exposes the client to the worst stimulus immediately — extinction. Both rely on the idea that no fear response is permanent without reinforcement.

Beck (1967): depressives hold negative schemas producing a negative triad — self, world, future — and distort information. Ellis's ABC (1962) says irrational Beliefs, not the Activating event itself, cause emotional Consequences. CBT challenges these.
